seo.metaDescription: Click on the below to find out more, or contact us direct to arrange a consultation at Sunshine Coast Oral, Facial & Implant Specialists

f3.value: What to expect, from first call to full recovery

f4.value: Everything you need before your consultation, before your surgery and in the days that follow.

f2.value: Your consultation is where we work out exactly what you need. Your surgeon will take a full history, examine your mouth and jaws, and arrange imaging. Most patients have an OPG or a 3D CBCT scan taken in our rooms on the day, so planning can begin immediately.

f3.value: You will leave with a clear explanation of your condition, the treatment options, the anaesthetic choices for your case, and a written, itemised treatment plan. Nothing is booked until you are ready.

f5.value: Your referral letter, if you have one

f6.value: Any recent x-rays, OPG or CBCT scans

f7.value: A list of current medications and any allergies

f8.value: Your Medicare card and private health fund details

f9.value: Your completed patient information form, if you have filled it in online

f11.value: Fees depend on the procedure, its complexity, and whether it is performed in our rooms or in hospital. Every patient receives a written quote with item numbers after their consultation so you can check rebates with your health fund before committing.

f13.value: Spread the cost of treatment across manageable instalments. Our patient coordinator will walk you through the plans available and what repayments look like for your case. Approval is subject to the provider's criteria.

f15.value: Extras cover often contributes to surgical fees. If your surgery is under general anaesthetic in hospital, your hospital cover may apply to theatre and anaesthetist costs. We provide item numbers so you can confirm your exact rebate.

f17.value: For major treatment such as full arch implants, eligible patients may apply to the ATO for early release of superannuation on compassionate grounds. We supply the clinical documentation. Eligibility is decided by the ATO.

f19.value: Some procedures attract a Medicare rebate. Hospital accommodation and anaesthetist fees are billed separately by the hospital and anaesthetist, and we will explain these before you book.

f22.value: For general anaesthetic or IV sedation, do not eat for six hours or drink clear fluids for two hours before your admission time, unless told otherwise

f23.value: Take your regular medications with a sip of water unless your surgeon or anaesthetist has advised you to stop them

f24.value: Arrange for a responsible adult to drive you home and stay with you overnight

f25.value: Wear loose, comfortable clothing and leave jewellery and valuables at home

f26.value: Let us know of any change in your health, including a cold or infection, before your surgery date

f28.value: Some swelling, bruising and discomfort is normal and usually peaks around day two or three before settling

f29.value: Use the pain relief plan you are sent home with and keep the surgical sites clean as instructed

f30.value: Stick to soft foods for the first few days and avoid smoking, alcohol and strenuous exercise while you heal

f31.value: Do not drive, operate machinery or sign legal documents for 24 hours after a general anaesthetic or sedation

f32.value: Call us straight away on {{phone}} if you have bleeding that will not settle, increasing pain, fever, or any concern at all

f33.value: You will receive written aftercare instructions specific to your procedure, and direct contact details for our team.

f35.value: Save time at your first visit by completing your patient information form before you arrive. If you prefer, the form can be completed in our rooms on the day.

f38.value: We welcome feedback about your experience. You can leave a Google review, or contact the practice manager directly on {{phone}}.

f40.value: Call us or send an enquiry and our patient coordinator will arrange your appointment with Dr Lincoln or Dr Higgins.

f43.value: Mon to Thu 8.00am to 5.00pm, Fri 8.00am to 4.00pm
